cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is partnership?
cards.back: When two or more persons join hands to set up a business and share its profits and losses, they are said to be in partnership.
cards.quote: When two or more persons join hands to set up a business and share its profits and losses, they are said to be in partnership.
reasons: review:Owner content call, 1 Nov 2026: near-duplicate of Define partnership (kept).

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: A document which contains the terms of partnership as agreed among the partners is called ‘Partnership ____’.
cards.back: A document which contains the terms of partnership as agreed among the partners is called ‘Partnership Deed’.
cards.quote: A document which contains the terms of partnership as agreed among the partners is called ‘Partnership Deed’.
reasons: review:DUPLICATE: same fact as kc.accountancy.partnership-fundamentals.def-deed-meaning. Same fact; kept is linked (duplicate sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: In which year is no interest on capital allowed to partners?
cards.back: Hence, no interest will be allowed during the year the firm has incurred net loss
cards.quote: Hence, no interest will be allowed during the year the firm has incurred net loss
reasons: review:DUPLICATE: same fact as kc.accountancy.profit-and-loss-appropriation-account.kl-ioc-only-profit. Same rule (no interest on capital in a loss year); kept has fuller quote and must importance (duplicate sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: As a sole proprietary business expands and needs more capital and people, which form of organisation do people usually adopt?
cards.back: As the business expands, one needs more capital and larger number of people to manage the business and share its risks. In such a situation, people usually adopt the partnership form of organisation.
cards.quote: As the business expands, one needs more capital and larger number of people to manage the business and share its risks. In such a situation, people usually adopt the partnership form of organisation.
reasons: review:Not important: introductory narrative filler with no testable point; the answer 'partnership' is given away by the chapter title.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Define partnership.
cards.back: Partnership is an agreement between two or more persons (called partners) for sharing the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
cards.quote: Partnership is an agreement between two or more persons (called partners) for sharing the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.
reasons: review:DUPLICATE: same fact as kc.accountancy.partnership-fundamentals.def-partnership-section-4, which quotes this chapter's own NCERT text (Section 4, Ch 1, p. 2); this line is from Ch 2, p. 48 (CTO content call, 1 Nov 2026).

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is the ratio called in which existing partners forgo shares and share the premium?
cards.back: This amount is shared by the existing partners in the ratio in which they forgo their shares in favour of the new partner which is called sacrificing ratio.
cards.quote: This amount is shared by the existing partners in the ratio in which they forgo their shares in favour of the new partner which is called sacrificing ratio.
reasons: review:DUPLICATE: same fact as kc.accountancy.admission-of-partner.def-sacrificing-ratio. Same definition; kept is linked (duplicate sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, ____ is passed in the books of the firm.
cards.back: If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm.
cards.quote: If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm.

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

reasons: review:Owner content call, 1 Nov 2026: reads oddly without its context.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: New partner does not bring goodwill in cash: which accounts are debited and credited?
cards.back: Goodwill not brought by the new partner will be debited to current account of new partner while sacrificing partners' capital accounts will be credited for their respective shares.
cards.quote: Goodwill not brought by the new partner will be debited to current account of new partner while sacrificing partners' capital accounts will be credited for their respective shares.

source.section: When the new partner does not bring goodwill

reasons: review:Redundant: same answer as fact-no-goodwill-books-credit-debit and fact-part-brought-current-debited; fronts hard to tell apart.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: When partners change their profit sharing ratio, how is the loss and gain in the value of goodwill adjusted?
cards.back: In such a situation, the loss and gain in the value of goodwill (if any) will have to be adjusted. This is done by crediting sacrificing partner’s and debiting gaining partner’s with appropriate amounts, as is explained earlier in the context of the admission of a new partners.
cards.quote: In such a situation, the loss and gain in the value of goodwill (if any) will have to be adjusted. This is done by crediting sacrificing partner’s and debiting gaining partner’s with appropriate amounts, as is explained earlier in the context of the admission of a new partners.

source.section: 2.9 Change in Profit Sharing Ratio among the Existing Partners

reasons: review:DUPLICATE: same fact as kc.accountancy.change-in-profit-sharing-ratio.fact-credit-sacrificing-debit-gaining. Same fact; kept is linked to far more questions (duplicate sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What happens to the partnership firm when a new partner is admitted?
cards.back: With the admission of a new partner, the partnership firm is reconstituted and a new agreement is entered into to carry on the business of the firm.
cards.quote: With the admission of a new partner, the partnership firm is reconstituted and a new agreement is entered into to carry on the business of the firm.
reasons: review:duplicate: old card def-reconstitution already states that any change ends the existing agreement and a new agreement comes into being.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Who decides the share of a new partner and how he acquires it from the existing partners?
cards.back: what will be the share of new partner and how he will acquire it from the existing partners is decided mutually among the old partners and the new partner.
cards.quote: But, what will be the share of new partner and how he will acquire it from the existing partners is decided mutually among the old partners and the new partner.
reasons: review:Front asks two things (who decides, and how he acquires it); the back only says 'mutually among the old partners and the new partner', so the 'how' part has no answer. Split or narrow to one question.

cards.back:
Goodwill A/c Dr.
To Sacrificing Partners Capital A/c
(Individually)(Goodwill distributed among the existing partners' in their sacrificing ratio)
cards.quote: Goodwill A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partners Capital A/c (Individually)(Goodwill distributed among the existing partners' in their sacrificing ratio).

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is done with unrecorded assets and liabilities of the firm at the time of admission?
cards.back: At times there may also be some unrecorded assets and liabilities of the firm. These also have to be brought into the books of the firm.
cards.quote: At times there may also be some unrecorded assets and liabilities of the firm. These also have to be brought into the books of the firm.

cards.front: Revaluation entries for a change in the value of an asset or liability: what amount is recorded?
cards.back: Entries (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are recorded only with the amount increase and decrease in the value of assets and liabilities.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Which special aspect of partnership accounts needs adjustment, and valuation if not specified, at reconstitution?
cards.back: Goodwill is also one of the special aspects of partnership accounts which requires adjustment (also valuation if not specified) at the time of reconstitution of a firm viz., a change in the profit sharing ratio, the admission of a partner or the retirement or death of a partner.
cards.quote: Goodwill is also one of the special aspects of partnership accounts which requires adjustment (also valuation if not specified) at the time of reconstitution of a firm viz., a change in the profit sharing ratio, the admission of a partner or the retirement or death of a partner.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: When a person pays for goodwill, what does he or she pay for?
cards.back: he/she pays for something, which places him in the position of being able to earn super profits as compared to the profit earned by other firms in the same industry.
cards.quote: It is generally observed that when a person pays for goodwill, he/she pays for something, which places him in the position of being able to earn super profits as compared to the profit earned by other firms in the same industry.
reasons: review:Open-ended: a student could say 'reputation' or 'an intangible', while the back wants a long phrase ('something which places him in the position of earning super profits'). No single fill.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Name the special advantages that raise the value of goodwill.
cards.back:
import licences
low rate and assured supply of electricity
long-term contracts for supply of materials
well-known collaborators
patents
trademarks
cards.quote: Special advantages: The firm that enjoys special advantages like import licences, low rate and assured supply of electricity, long-term contracts for supply of materials, well-known collaborators, patents, trademarks, etc. enjoy higher value of goodwill.

source.section: 2.5.2 Factors Affecting the Value of Goodwill

reasons: review:NCERT's list is non-exhaustive ('like ... etc.'); the back drops 'etc.', so a student naming another advantage cannot be judged. Better as a key_line with blanks or a 'which of these' framing.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Define an intangible asset under AS 26.
cards.back: Intangible Asset under AS 26 is defined as an identifiable, non monetary, without physical existence and held for use in the production or supply of goods or services for rental to others or for administrative purposes.
cards.quote: As per the Standard, Intangible Asset under AS 26 is defined as an identifiable, non monetary, without physical existence and held for use in the production or supply of goods or services for rental to others or for administrative purposes.

source.section: Applicability of Accounting Standard 26: Intangible Assets

reasons: review:AS 26 definition is outside the CUET Unit II goodwill list (nature, factors, methods); quote wording is also garbled ('identifiable, non monetary, without physical existence and held for use ...').

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Under AS 26, over what period should intangible assets be written off?
cards.back: Intangible assets should be written off as early as possible but not exceeding its estimated life, which normally should not be beyond 10 years.
cards.quote: Intangible assets should be written off as early as possible but not exceeding its estimated life, which normally should not be beyond 10 years.

source.section: Applicability of Accounting Standard 26: Intangible Assets

reasons: review:AS 26 detail outside the CUET goodwill sub-topics; trivia for a CUET student.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What can an economist judge, and what do governmental actions rest on, through analysis of the financial statements of various firms?
cards.back: Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector.

Operating Profit before Working Capital changes
Add : in case of increase in current assets (other than cash and cash xxx equivalent) and decrease in current liabilities.

– Income Tax Paid
+/– Effects of Extraordinary Items
Net Cash from Operating Activities
